sources.claim_ceiling: Human comparative signal in the exact chronic-wound study population and intervention context; not universal effectiveness or cross-device equivalence.
limitations: 35 participants per arm.
CAP was used alongside best-practice wound care.
A study-specific result does not establish equivalence across wound etiologies or devices.
A reported wound-area result is not a universal complete-healing or recurrence guarantee.

sources.claim_ceiling: A review-level comparative signal across included chronic-wound RCTs; heterogeneity and risk of bias limit transfer and certainty.
limitations: The review included 12 RCTs and 477 participants.
Intervention devices, protocols and wound populations varied.
The authors identify heterogeneity and study-quality limitations.
Source-specific pooled estimates must not be reinterpreted as device-specific treatment effects.

sources.claim_ceiling: Early wound-area signal and short-term safety observations in the included DFU RCTs; not proof of durable infection control or general wound effectiveness.
limitations: Only three RCTs, 107 participants and 126 ulcers were included.
No sustained between-group bacterial-load advantage was reported.
No serious treatment-related adverse events were reported in the included trials; this does not prove absence of risk.
Larger and longer randomized studies were recommended.

sources.claim_ceiling: Existence and design of a Phase III clinical-trial protocol, with recruitment reported complete and final sample size 141; no Phase III clinical outcome or efficacy claim.
limitations: The registry update of 2026-10-08 reports recruitment complete and study continuing; no Phase III results are posted.
The planned sample size was 140 and the register reports final sample size 141.
This is prevention of radiation dermatitis during breast radiotherapy, not treatment of the tumour.
Earlier Phase I/II summaries in the registry are not Phase III outcome evidence.
Protocol and recruitment status do not establish clinical benefit, device authorization or routine clinical use.

sources.claim_ceiling: Evidence synthesis dominated by preclinical results; the review reports only one short-term human randomized trial and says routine clinical use remains preliminary.
limitations: 19 studies: 11 in vitro, 7 animal and 1 human randomized trial.
A single short-term human trial is insufficient to establish routine clinical use.
Direct CAP and plasma-activated liquids appear in the review and are not interchangeable interventions.
No blanket safety conclusion should be transferred to unstudied exposure conditions.

sources.claim_ceiling: A small Phase I human safety/feasibility signal for a specific intraoperative surgical-margin intervention; not general antitumour efficacy, survival benefit or systemic immunotherapy evidence.
limitations: 20 patients with advanced or recurrent solid tumours were reported.
The primary study objective was safety.
The intervention followed macroscopic tumour resection and was limited to the surgical setting described.
The study is not a randomized efficacy trial.
FDA IDE authorization for a clinical investigation is not marketing clearance or approval.

sources.claim_ceiling: Existence and design of a Phase I PAW wound-rinse protocol; no clinical safety or efficacy outcome.
limitations: Protocol only; no trial results are claimed.
PAW is an indirect liquid-delivery intervention, not direct CAP exposure.
Liquid composition, storage, time-dependent chemistry and biological matrix need independent characterization.

sources.claim_ceiling: A proposed physical/biological dosimetry framework and synthesis of heterogeneous literature; not a validated universal clinical dose standard.
limitations: The review discusses more than 400 studies.
It proposes volumetric RONS flux and redox-homeostatic status as complementary indices.
The proposal is not a universal calibrated clinical dosing standard.
Device, tissue, modality and biological-response heterogeneity remain substantial.

sources.claim_ceiling: Study-specific randomized comparative result: numerically greater wound-area reduction but no statistically significant superiority to standard care on the primary week-17 wound-area endpoint; immediate microbial-burden reductions were observed.
limitations: 60 adults with nonhealing venous leg ulcers were randomized in an open-label multicentre study.
At week 17, mean wound-area reduction was -72.9% with CAPJ versus -56.7% with standard care, but the difference was not statistically significant (P=0.30).
Complete healing was 42.9% versus 30.4% (P=0.361).
CAPJ produced significant immediate microbial-burden reductions at weeks 0 and 4.
No serious device-attributed adverse events were reported; transient pain-related sensations were the most frequent treatment-related effects.
This result is not evidence of equivalence or proof of no benefit, and does not transfer to other wound etiologies or CAP devices.

sources.claim_ceiling: The institutional technology catalogue identifies kINPen MED as a commercially available Class IIa medical device and lists source specifications; catalogue data is not independent comparative clinical performance evidence.
limitations: Catalogue-listed power is below 3.5 W at 1 MHz with argon flow 4–6 standard L/min and reported temperature 35–38 °C.
The catalogue describes a small-area plasma jet and identifies chronic wounds and pathogen-induced skin diseases as medical-use areas.
Catalogue specifications are not a matched head-to-head performance result or a Luminous measurement.
A device-specific class IIa statement from this catalogue is not a substitute for jurisdiction-specific authorization verification.

sources.claim_ceiling: Short-term human comparative signal in the exact studied Wagner grade 2 DFU population and helium CAP protocol; does not establish long-term complete closure, recurrence prevention, limb preservation, or transfer to other devices and wound etiologies.
notable_findings: The study assigned 50 participants to standard care or standard care plus helium-based CAP.
CAP was applied twice weekly for three weeks; wound size and targeted bacterial cultures were assessed at baseline and days 7, 14 and 21.
Authors reported wound contraction of 1.21 cm/day versus 0.79 cm/day and bacterial-load reduction of 32.8% versus 10.0% for CAP plus standard care versus standard care.
limitations: Open-label design.
Only 50 participants and one study.
The population was limited to Wagner grade 2 DFUs.
Reported measurements ended at day 21; durable complete closure, recurrence, amputation and long-term safety are not established.
The study was published after the 2010–2025 search window described by the 2026 chronic-wound meta-analysis and must not be silently counted among its 12 RCTs.
The authors declare no competing interests; two authors are affiliated with a plasma technology company, which should remain visible as contextual provenance without inferring undisclosed conflict.

sources.claim_ceiling: Preclinical characterization of a specific helium multijet research source under its declared test conditions; does not establish clinical efficacy, a clinical indication, regulatory authorization or a transferable biological dose.
notable_findings: Two- and four-outlet applicators were evaluated with active surface treatment area, evaporation, ex-vivo porcine-skin temperature, electrical characterization, in-vitro cytotoxicity and micronucleus/genotoxicity testing.
At 10 mm and four minutes, the paper reports full active surface treatment area of 1,311 mm² for the two-jet applicator and 787 mm² for the four-jet applicator.
At 8 mm the four-jet result was 540 mm² versus 443 mm² for the two-jet applicator, a 22% difference under the reported assay conditions.
Short-exposure blind spots between plume targets and geometry-dependent thermal effects were reported.
The authors reported no increase in micronuclei relative to untreated control in the tested HaCaT assay and limited cytotoxicity under the studied conditions.
limitations: A single research device and study protocol; no independent multi-laboratory replication is established by this source record.
KI-starch active-area mapping is a spatial screening measure and not species-specific RONS dosimetry or biological-dose measurement.
The 2-jet/4-jet area results are specific to the paper's geometry, assay threshold, distance and time; they are not universal scaling coefficients.
Ex-vivo and in-vitro safety findings do not establish human clinical safety or efficacy.
No human participants or clinical trial outcomes.
